item.title: Tourists out of the picture as VIPs view da Vinci masterpiece
item.description: Tourists to Milan during the Winter Olympics hoping to see Leonardo da Vinci’s The Last Supper were in for an unwelcome surprise: Access to the masterpiece is closed to the public for three-and-a-half days. Source: Crux.

item.title: Hong Kong Catholic activist sentenced to 20 years in prison
item.description: Human rights advocate and Catholic Jimmy Lai was sentenced in Hong Kong yesterday to 20 years in prison over what Chinese officials claim were national security violations. Source: EWTN News.

item.title: US archbishop to be beatified after six-year pause
item.description: United States archbishop and evangelist Venerable Fulton Sheen will soon be beatified, now that the Vatican has given the green light, the Diocese of Peoria, Illinois, announced yesterday. Source: OSV News.

item.title: Handmade rosaries offer support for hospital patients and families
item.description: About 450 rosaries handmade by volunteers from Parramatta parishes, agencies, schools and the Diocesan Chancery have been shared with patients and families in Western Sydney hospitals. Source: Catholic Outlook.

item.title: Caritas presents prayers of solidarity to Papal Nuncio
item.description: Caritas Australia has presented a collection of nearly 900 messages of prayer, solidarity and hope from the Australian Catholic community to the Apostolic Nuncio to Australia, Archbishop Charles Balvo.

item.title: Antisemitism royal commission may investigate Indigenous racism
item.description: Indigenous Australians Minister Malarndirri McCarthy says she will encourage people to put in submissions to the antisemitism royal commission about racism against Indigenous Australians. Source: The Australian.

item.title: Hobart Archdiocese successfully embeds safeguarding in its culture
item.description: Hobart Archdiocese’s latest safeguarding audit showed the archdiocese has successfully embedded safeguarding within its culture and demonstrated a commitment to ensuring the Church is a safe place for children and adults at risk of abuse. Source: ACSL.

item.title: Vinnies welcomes Bishops’ Social Justice Statement
item.description: As inflation and interest rates rise, the St Vincent de Paul Society has welcomed the Australian Catholic Bishops Conference’s latest Social Justice Statement, which highlights the worsening cost‑of‑living crisis facing millions of people on low and modest incomes.

item.title: Pope to visit Sydney for Eucharist28
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will visit Sydney in the spring of 2028 to preside over the International Eucharistic Congress. Source: The Catholic Weekly.
